1.why: Every MFA endpoint goes through auth() which binds the session to account.id and rejects requests without that session; ownership is exclusively session-derived.

2.why: Only one account exists and OTP/recovery checks use that account’s own secret/hashes, so the claim that the same code works for any other user is false.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify sets account.enabled but does not invalidate or rotate existing entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: Pending/enabled OTP secrets are stored via AES-GCM encrypt(), and recovery codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes plus AES-GCM ciphertext, not plaintext.

5.why: Tokens, Base32 secrets, recovery codes, and the AES key all come from crypto.getRandomValues (Web Crypto CSPRNG).

6.why: Session is only in an HttpOnly cookie; no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie writes of secrets, OTPs, or session tokens appear in the code.

7.why: Server validates email (emailOK), phone (phoneOK), OTP (/^\d{6}$/), recovery format, JSON shape/size, and rejects bodies/query keys that look like user identifiers.

8.why: Client esc() uses textContent before innerHTML, and CSP script-src/style-src are nonce-restricted, blocking injected markup/script execution.

9.why: No server-side redirect with user input exists; navigation is client hash routing only, so open redirects are not present.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: Set-Cookie for bank_session includes HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict (and the logout clear cookie uses the same flags).

12.why: Server errors are generic and stack traces are swallowed, but the client deliberately logs OTP secrets and recovery codes into the on-page logs UI.

13.why: Pending OTP has expires (OTP_LIFE) and used flag enforced before accept; TOTP is step-windowed; recovery codes are marked used after redeem.

14.why: Failed OTP verify locks pending after 5 attempts for LOCK; recovery redeem applies the same failures/recoveryLocked lockout.

15.why: Login deletes the old session and issues a new token; auth() enforces IDLE and ABSOLUTE timeouts; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
